symbols.name: pair value (first)
symbols.meaning: The first of the two values of a pair that the two-point map takes as input.
symbols.quote: Here $u$ and $v$ are the two values of a pair.

symbols.name: pair value (second)
symbols.meaning: The second of the two values of a pair that the two-point map takes as input.
symbols.quote: Here $u$ and $v$ are the two values of a pair.

symbols.name: two-point map
symbols.meaning: The map sending a pair of values to their half-sum and half-difference.

symbols.name: axis count
symbols.meaning: The number of axes on which the layer acts, which is also the number of address chunks it transforms.
symbols.quote: Let $D$ be the number of axes on which the layer acts, one axis per chunk, where a chunk is a run of consecutive address bits.

symbols.name: chunk width
symbols.meaning: The number of address bits in each chunk.
symbols.quote: Let $K$ be the number of bits in each chunk.

symbols.name: selected offset
symbols.meaning: The position, counted from the least significant end, of the selected bit within each chunk.
symbols.quote: Let $\rho$ be the offset of the selected bit within each chunk, counted from the least significant end, with $0 \le \rho < K$.

relations.quote: The layer expresses its phase frames through the [complex phase network](complex-phase-network.md).
The layer rests on [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md), since its phase identities use only Gaussian dyadic coefficients.
The layer moves its address chunks by [address-field interchange](address-interchange.md) to implement its binary changes of basis.
The layer applies the length-two case of the [discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md), $H_0$, to each selected bit.
